_comment: wallpaperscraft.com, described 2026-10-16 from the site as it answers from this machine.
ROBOTS: 'User-agent: * / Allow: / / Disallow: /search / Crawl-delay: 1.0'. So the text search box
is off (ask=false, same rule as 4kwallpapers, whose /search is disallowed too), and the interval is
set to 2000 ms - double the crawl-delay they ask for.
THE TRICK THIS SITE PLAYS ON A RECON: it answers with gzip even to a client that never asked for it
(the first 8 KB of every page here start with 1f 8b). Read raw, the homepage looks like an empty
shell with no links and no pictures; decompressed it is 54 KB with 124 links and 15 cards.
WHAT IS LISTABLE: /all/<resolution> is a server-rendered grid of 15 cards and nothing else is -
/catalog/<topic> answers 200 with 0 cards in that markup (it is a topic landing page), and
/all/<resolution>?page=2 answers 404. So one visit is 15 pictures, no paging, which is what the
grid shows. The card's own link names the rung it is offered at, so `size` and the file url are
both built from the data rather than from an invented low/mid/high.
THE FULL-SIZE FILE is the thumbnail's url with the size swapped: the card prints
…/image/single/ocean_shore_slope_1728510_300x168.jpg and the file at the same place with
_3840x2160.jpg answers 200 image/jpeg 1,280,551 bytes (measured). Dropping 'single/' 404s, and the
/download/<name>/<rung> link in the card is an html page, not the file - both were tried.
resolution values are the site's own desktop rungs (it publishes 44 in all, including portrait and
square ones); the list here is every landscape rung from 720p up.
